chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr and others from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I combined [the Umrah and Hajj] this year and brought the sacrificial animal.' He said: 'Why did you do that? The Tamattu' is better, by Allah. Do not return [to doing Qiran].'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a form of Hajj where Umrah is performed separately before Hajj)
key_terms.قَرَنْتُ: I combined (referring to Qiran, a form of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with one body)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qiran and Tamattu' in Hajj and which is preferred?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the superiority of *Tamattu'* over *Qiran* for those who can afford the sacrificial animal (*Hady*), emphasizing that the pilgrim should not repeat the same form if a better option exists. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that *Tamattu'* is the most recommended form of Hajj due to its distinct rituals and spiritual benefits, provided the pilgrim has the means. The narration highlights the practical guidance given to companions regarding the optimal performance of Hajj rites.
